catalogRevisions.note: X5: the Rust catalog revision per mode. Changing the catalog requires updating these reviewed values (crate test catalog::tests::revisions_match_manifest).

D10.summary: With standalone mutations disabled, Rust runs only tools whose effect is read instead of Go's enumerated gate list

D11.summary: Rust rejects enumerated invalid MCP calls without invocation audit writes; Go remains unchanged

D12.summary: Rust refuses task-aware calls at binding or admission before any durable operation record; Go persists the operation first (server.go:1642-1652)

D13.summary: Rust's redact_for_storage fails closed on any unmarked/open-schema durable content, replacing it with a redaction marker; Go's pinned reference persists it verbatim. Delivery to a caller (tasks/get, live or restored) is unaffected by this divergence.

D14.summary: Every Rust capability, built-in or external, follows one architecture: a Service Definition, a Service Provider mounted in one service context, and a Consumer; they differ only in distribution, trust and declared Go-observable contracts; built-in identities are unreachable by provider families; no observable change; M1-M7 capabilities are revised onto the seam before M8 starts

D8.summary: Rust implements the stricter oauth-issuance contract instead of Go's token issuance

go-vs-go.purpose: harness self-validation: the pinned Go binary compared with itself must be clean and deterministic

go-vs-rust.purpose: T1 differential parity of the Rust candidate; items outside a gate's surfaces may fail until their milestone

cutover.description: Whole-agent cutover (task 6.1). Fails until every surface has passing Rust evidence and the inventory has no gaps, owned or not; later milestones add T2/T3/T4 suites here

m0.description: M0 exit: harness proven (Go-vs-Go clean x20, every canary caught), inventory captured with zero unowned gaps, every Rust item present and unverified

m1.description: M1 exit: harness valid (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory) and the Rust candidate matches Go on every CLI, config and lifecycle item (x5), and passes the Go black-box startup tests; other surfaces may still differ (M2+)

m2.description: M2 exit: harness valid (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory); the Rust candidate matches Go on every CLI, config, lifecycle, HTTP, MCP wire and auth item (x5), including the generated wire corpus and the authz store cross-read; the Go black-box tests and the go-sdk real client pass against Rust; other surfaces may still differ (M3+); the declared divergence D8 (oauth-issuance) passes its Rust contract suite and every Rust canary is caught

m3.description: M3 exit: harness valid (Go-vs-Go x20, canaries, inventory); the Rust candidate publishes every catalog cell identically to Go (names, descriptors, schemas, edges, revision) and matches Go on every scenario of every surface (x5), including the read-only host tools, argument validation, the standalone mutation set and the X2 rejected-call invariant; the go-sdk real client reads the catalog and calls read-only tools; the D8 and D10 contract suites and Rust canaries pass; catalog revisions match the reviewed manifest (X5)

m4.description: M4 exit: everything M3 requires, plus admission and tasks matching Go on every scenario (x5): canonical URIs and kinds, tenant scope, the admission matrix over every non-read tool (gate closed, stale revision, binding, unknown target) with X2, coordinator saturation N+k, min-memory/min-disk headroom, normal-class host reads, the task registry, input_required, and cancellation before start, mid-shim and after completion with zero orphans; the D12 contract suite and its Rust canaries pass

m5.description: M5 exit: M1-M4 regression gates plus all six provenance-bound durable-state and redaction validations; missing evidence fails closed.

m6.description: M6 exit: M1-M5 regression gates plus the single plan executor -- recipe/plan validation (valid and invalid corpora), execution-trace fault scripts (retry-then-success, permanent-failure-with-compensation, readiness-never-true-timeout, cancel-mid-node) and restart-mid-plan reconcile -- all matching Go byte-for-byte except the declared, scoped-out probe_http_endpoint cancellation-framing note in evidence/m6/README.md (not a Rust/Go behavioral divergence requiring a decision: both sides now interrupt a cancelled in-flight dispatch promptly, masked only on the exact terminal literal).

goReference.note: CGO_ENABLED=0, -trimpath, -buildvcs=false, fixed ldflags; reproducible for a given Go toolchain

rustCandidate.note: Hash of the binary that produced evidence/current; rebuild and rerun make parity-m1 after any Rust change.
